heuristic.applicability: Prefer buffer_red__h04 when red is translated relative to its demonstrated initial patch, the supplied free buffer is translated, or the overlap blue object is translated, provided the observed state clearly matches red acquisition, red transport/release, or blue overlap and the relevant poses remain reachable. During red acquisition the positional action is anchored to observed red; during carry/release it is anchored to the supplied buffer; during overlap it is anchored to observed blue. Prefer validated buffer_red__h02 instead when phase is ambiguous, an object is unexpectedly elevated/dropped, the buffer may be occupied, or the deterministic anchor rule is doubtful. h04 is not a recovery policy.

handoff.entry_conditions: Gripper open and TCP high/clear for normal entry, with observed red on or near the initially blue region and not held. Intermediate entry is applicable only when causal geometry clearly supports one supervised phase: low/open approach to red, closed and visibly elevated red transport, low buffered-red release/retreat, or red stable in the buffer with transit/acquisition of blue. Object poses, supplied buffer pose and measured Panda configuration must be finite and plausibly reachable.
handoff.exit_conditions: Core exit guidance is unchanged: red is visibly settled in the supplied free buffer, fingers are open, and TCP is clear. The supervised later exit may occur with red stationary in the buffer and blue, not red, beneath closed fingers and beginning to lift. Final task success remains red_at_goal AND blue_at_goal and is not redefined by this policy.
handoff.failure_signatures: Wrong anchor switching is distinctive: targets move toward the buffer before red is visibly elevated, remain red-anchored after release, or move toward blue before red is stable. Other signatures are a closed-finger miss, red not following the TCP, red entering then leaving the buffer, red elevated after opening, repeated gripper toggles, or persistent IK nonconvergence/limit contact. Successful demonstrations do not establish recovery from these states.
handoff.overlap_role: All assigned labels are retained through the 210-230 action overlap with place_blue. The adaptive anchor remains buffer-relative during red lowering/opening and early retreat, then becomes blue-relative for transit, blue approach/closure and initial lift. This keeps the receiving phase action-supervised while avoiding use of released red as the positional anchor.
handoff.successor_readiness: Switch to place_blue once red is observed stable in the supplied buffer and fingers/TCP are open and clear. A later switch after blue closure and visible initial lift is also supervised. Preserve both causal frames across the switch; neither an anchor mode nor an auxiliary phase prediction is proof of grasp or release.

heuristic.limitations: The by-construction invariant is phase-local Cartesian position under displacement of the selected anchor; it does not make Panda posture, reachability, collision geometry, contact, dynamics, travel length or TCP orientation invariant. Orientation is a chunk-start TCP world rotation-vector residual. The deterministic phase rule has no contact truth and can misclassify elevated-but-unheld, dropped, occluded/noisy or occupied-buffer states. It is frozen for each sampled chunk, so transitions inside a chunk use the prior anchor until replanning. Large rotations/translations can be unreachable or unsupported. There are no failed-grasp/drop recovery demonstrations and no out-of-distribution validation. Use h02 for ambiguous-phase cases rather than assuming h04 recovers.
heuristic.pipeline_implications: Add buffer_red__h04 as an independently trained library option, without modifying h01-h03. The high-level selector supplies the current reachable buffer pose and chooses h04 for clearly phased spatial displacement; h02 remains the default evidence-backed option for demonstrated geometry or uncertain phase because it passed 12/12 in-distribution runs. Monitor fresh object geometry and IK diagnostics at each replan, but do not treat them as success. Preserve H2 history across switches and use the unchanged red-stable/open-clear handoff rule.
heuristic.rationale: Observed demonstrations use sampled red and blue starts but a common sequence: red approach/closure, lift/transport, buffer lower/open/retreat, then blue acquisition/lift. In demo10100 and demo10103, commanded positions follow each differently located red during indices 40-160, converge on the buffer around 200-280, and follow each differently located blue around 380-479. Validation observed h02 at 12/12 final containment, fixed red anchoring h01 at 5/12, and fixed buffer anchoring h03 at 0/12; no OOD result exists. h04 therefore retains h02's 7D TCP-orientation residual, trainable two-frame encoder and phase auxiliary objective, but uses one semantic positional anchor at a time rather than forcing red or buffer to parameterize all phases. The falsifiable expected benefit is improved transfer to translations of the phase-relevant red, buffer, or blue while avoiding the fixed-anchor burden. This benefit is unconfirmed and h04 may underperform h02 if deterministic switches or local labels are harder to learn.
heuristic.statement: Phase-adaptive semantic-anchor Diffusion Policy: predict TCP target position in the observed red frame for red acquisition/initial lift, in the supplied buffer frame for carry/lowering/release, and in the observed blue frame for the supervised overlap; predict TCP orientation as a chunk-start world rotation residual and retain the native gripper scalar. A causal deterministic mode selects the position anchor per chunk, while a learned two-frame encoder shared with a four-class phase auxiliary head conditions the unchanged standard diffusion backbone.

assignment.subgoal: From an open, clear gripper with red in the initially blue region, approach red from above, close around it, lift and carry it to the free central area, lower it to the table, open, and retreat. The core responsibility is red-to-buffer relocation. The tail is deliberately extended through approach, grasp, and initial lift of blue so a late handoff remains action-supervised.

check.checkpoint_selection: last EMA at the declared update budget

conversion_check.description: Command FK position is encoded with inverse active-anchor rotation/translation and exactly recomposed; command orientation is encoded by the SO(3) log relative to chunk-start TCP and recomposed by the exponential map. The independent check compares world TCP position, rotation and gripper after shared IK.

contract.cut_relation: Every assigned action in all 12 [0,stop) segments supervises semantic-anchor diffusion and a causal phase target. The 210-230 action overlap with place_blue remains action-supervised from red lowering/release through blue acquisition and initial lift.
contract.output_semantics: Each slot is [anchor_x,anchor_y,anchor_z,rotvec_x,rotvec_y,rotvec_z,gripper]. The first three values are a target TCP position in metres in the chunk-frozen active anchor: observed red for phase 0 acquisition/initial lift, supplied buffer for phases 1-2 transport/release, and observed blue for phase 3 overlap. rotvec is radians for R_target*R_chunk_tcp^T in world axes. The decoder composes the frozen semantic position anchor and chunk-start TCP orientation, then calls panda_kinematics.solve_ik from fresh measured qpos; gripper sign is native. Slots are t-1..t+14 and slots 1..8 execute.
contract.parameter_semantics: target_object selects the observed red pose used as the acquisition position anchor and phase object; successor_object selects the observed blue pose used as the overlap position anchor; buffer_pose_world is [x,y,z,qw,qx,qy,qz] in world metres/wxyz and supplies the intended free-center transport/release anchor. Training binds [-0.181,0,0.02,1,0,0,0]. All three arguments enter causal features, anchor selection, encoding and decoding.
